# BookShelf: overview

A personal library tracker where readers register, sign in, and keep a list of the books they own with title, author, ISBN and reading status. It is an ASP.NET Core MVC prototype (type: web, status: prototype).

## Stack and structure

- **Language and framework:** C# on ASP.NET Core MVC (net8.0) with Razor views.
- **Data:** Entity Framework Core with SQL Server (`AppDbContext` in `Data/`).
- **Entry point:** `Program.cs`.
- **Key folders:** `Controllers/` (HTTP controllers), `Views/` (Razor views), `Models/` (entities), `Data/` (DbContext).

## Screens (6)

| Id | Name | Purpose |
|----|------|---------|
| `home-index` | Home | Landing page with links to sign in and create an account |
| `account-login` | Login | Sign in with email and password |
| `account-register` | Register | Create an account with email and password |
| `books-index` | My Books | List the books with title, author and status |
| `books-details` | Book Details | Show one book with a delete action |
| `books-create` | Add a Book | Form to add a book |

The shared layout (`Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`) is not a screen.

## Data

Three entities: `User` (Id, Email, PasswordHash), `Book` (Id, Title, Author, Isbn, Status, UserId) and `Review` (Id, BookId, Rating, Text). The links between them are inferred from the `UserId` and `BookId` field names.

## Routes

11 routes across `HomeController`, `AccountController` (login, register, logout) and `BooksController` (list, details, create, delete). The full list is in `profile.json`.

## Risks

- Sign-in does not check credentials (TODO in the login handler), and registration does not create a user.
- Book pages have no `[Authorize]`, and book queries are not filtered by user.
- `Review` has an entity but no controller, route or view.
- No automated tests were found.

## Confidence: medium

Derived from code only; the README is three lines. All controllers, models and the DbContext were read; Razor views other than `Books/Index` were not. Key assumptions: Reader is the only actor, `Book.Status` has values beyond the default "To read", and flow steps come from controller redirects.

## What was generated

Wireframes for all 6 screens plus three state variants, a screen-flow map, architecture, flow, sequence and ER diagrams, 13 user stories, and a 3-sprint plan (43 points). See the folders next to this file.
